name: Deficiencies
rows: Fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 · USD · Internal control walkthrough workpapers
DRAFT FOR THE CPA · walkthroughs and limited testing · not an examination of internal control · no opinion

Significant deficiency, proposed (P2P-1, P2P-2, ITG-1). Mei Northcott, Accounts Payable Specialist, can set up vendors and approve payments. She set up Marten Lake Aggregates LLC, Rainier Site Supply LLC, Sound Formwork Rentals LLC without approval and approved 4 payments to them herself, $64,675.50, each under her portal limit. The invoices are for job materials and nothing suggests the vendors are not real, but the controls that would stop a fictitious vendor were bypassed. Recommendation: remove her approval permission in the bank portal; have the Controller approve every vendor setup and bank change before payment; review the vendor change report monthly; confirm the three vendors’ bank details by calling a number on file; review system access every year.

Significant deficiency, proposed (CLS-1). 30 manual entries over $25,000, $8,045,083.44, were prepared and posted by the Controller with no second review, including accruals, depreciation and the over and under billings. The quarterly review later found September interest was never accrued (INT-01), the kind of error a second review catches. Recommendation: the Chief Financial Officer reviews and initials the Controller’s entries over the threshold before posting, turn on the system’s approval step, and sign a monthly close checklist. The CPA considers whether this and SOD-01 together are a material weakness.

Deficiency, proposed (PAY-1, PAY-2). Renata Salazar, Payroll and HR Manager, can edit the payroll master and process payroll; she entered her own raise, $88,000.00 to $98,000.00, before the form was signed, and $4,999.93 more was paid to June 30 (the payroll audit’s RATE-01). The Controller’s review sees totals only, and the master file change report is never run. Recommendation: run the change report every payroll and have the Controller review and sign it; the President and CEO signs PAF-25-119 or the pay is corrected.

Deficiency, proposed (CLS-2). All 12 operating account reconciliations were prepared on time and reconcile, and June ties to the trial balance, but none is signed as reviewed. The cash audit found the same in the company’s June reconciliation. Recommendation: the Controller signs and dates each reconciliation within the 15 days and follows up any item older than 60 days.

The machine proposes each level from what could go wrong, how much flows through the control and whether another control catches it. The CPA decides every level and whether SOD-01 and JE-01 together are a material weakness.
